title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 566-568, from the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'). Grothendieck is identifying a group-theoretically defined set with the solution set of a 'loop equation'.

The group-theoretic side:
- S_0Γ_{ρ,σ} is a fibre product of triples x=(u,a,b).
- u lies in Z_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(𝔖^+)×Ẑ^*×{±1}×{±1}: an automorphism of the profinite group 𝔖^+ together with a cyclotomic-type character μ and two signs ε', ε. Here 𝔖 is a profinite group with distinguished elements ρ, σ, an involution τ', and a distinguished element ε_1 (or ε_0).
- a and b lie in the 'special' normalizers SN*_ρ and SN*_σ of ρ and σ, compatible with u.

The equation side: SG^{ff}_{ρ,σ} is the set of triples (α,β,μ) in 𝔖×𝔖×Ẑ^* satisfying [α,ρ]=[β,σ]·ε_1^{μ-1}.

On p.566 the map (75) is x ↦ (α,β,μ), with α = u a^{-1} τ'^{ν'}, β = u b^{-1} τ'^{ν} and μ = χ(x). It is shown to be injective: from (α,β,μ) one recovers ν', ν, μ, then u, then a and b.

This page proves surjectivity of the injection (79) S_0Γ_{ρ,σ} ↪ SG^{ff}_{ρ,σ}. The argument is a standard torsor/orbit argument in three steps.
1. Compose (79) with the projection SG^{ff} → Σ^{ff}_{ρ,σ} ≅ Z_{ρ,σ}. By (77)-(78) the composite is formula (80): x ↦ (ξ=[u,ρ], η=[u,σ], μ, ε', ε), where u(ρ)=ξρ and u(σ)=ησ. Under Σ^{ff} ≅ Z_{ρ,σ} this is just the projection (u,a,b) ↦ u. That projection is surjective because SN*_ρ × SN*_σ = SZ_ρ × SZ_σ, so suitable a, b always exist.
2. Introduce (81), the right action of SN_ρ×SN_σ (= SZ_ρ×SZ_σ) on SG_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Γ̂×Γ̂×Ẑ^*, given by (α,β,μ) ↦ (αa_0, βb_0, μ). This action is free, and its quotient is Σ_{ρ,σ} (similarly for the starred versions).
3. Next page: with ε, ε' fixed, this action corresponds under (75)/(76) to (u,a,b) ↦ (u, τ^{ν'}(a_0^{-1})a, τ^{ν}(b_0^{-1})b), i.e. a left translation on the (a,b) coordinates. So the injection is equivariant for compatible free actions and surjective on orbit spaces, hence bijective; this is (84). Dividing by the left translation action of L_0 (ℓ acts by (α,β,μ) ↦ (ℓα, ℓβ, μ)) gives (86): Γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ L_0\SG^{ff}_{ρ,σ}.

Purpose: to describe an automorphism-type group Γ_{ρ,σ}, automorphisms preserving the conjugacy classes of two distinguished elements, modulo inner ones, as the solution set of a commutator equation. This is the familiar mechanism by which GT-type groups are presented by pairs (λ,f) satisfying relations.
errors: The surjectivity proof is only sketched: freeness of (81) is asserted ('il est clair'). Equivariance of (79) with respect to the twisted action is only established on the next page via the τ'^{ν} twists, which are needed because N_ρ may invert ρ.
Grothendieck's own page numbering (566-588) is inconsistent across neighbouring pages, apparently a renumbering in the manuscript.

ideas.what: Proving bijectivity of an injective map between two sets with compatible free group actions by checking surjectivity on orbit spaces (quotients identified with Z_{ρ,σ} ≅ Σ_{ρ,σ}).

Identification of the group of (outer) automorphisms of a profinite group preserving conjugacy classes of distinguished elements ρ, σ (with cyclotomic character μ) with the solution set of a loop/commutator equation [α,ρ]=[β,σ]ε_1^{μ-1}, modulo left translation by L_0.
ideas.modern_name: presentation of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type groups by pairs (λ,f) satisfying relations
ideas.where_published: Only the program in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the 'équation des lacets' notes are unpublished

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine step (the surjectivity half of a bijection) inside a longer computation. The surrounding dossier, Grothendieck's own loop-equation description of Teichmüller-type groups, is of historical interest. This page adds nothing beyond a standard orbit argument.
transcription_corrections: 'S𝒢^{#}' and 'Σ^{#}' should read S𝒢^{ff} / Σ^{ff} (the 'eff/ff' superscript used on neighbouring pages).
The arrow label read 'ip' is probably 'pr' (canonical projection).
In (81) the condition should read [α,ρ]=[β,σ] ε_1^{μ-1}, not 'ε,μ^{-1}'.
'qui est surjective, au moyen SN*...' is more likely 'vu que SN*_ρ×SN*_σ = SZ_ρ×SZ_σ'; the marginal '(=SZ_ρ×SZ_σ)' attaches to SN_ρ×SN_σ in (81).
In (81) the hat-Γ factors are written as 𝔖 (script S) in the manuscript, consistent with neighbouring pages.
The line 'd'où on a le résultat ... Or, pour' and the start of (82) are largely crossed out; the surviving formula is (u,a,b) ↦ (u, ε_ρ^{τ'}(a_0^{-1})a, ε_σ^{τ'}(b_0^{-1})b).
